reader_question: How sure is each of the five topic hubs’ evidence?
grade_line: Graded by the atlas, claim by claim: our count of its register of claims
title: Of the atlas’s five topic hubs, “Public services where you live” has the largest share of documented claims, 84.5 percent.
measure_line: Claims behind the atlas’s 16 everyday answers, grouped by its five topic hubs, as a share of each hub’s claims by evidence grade, 433 claims as of the atlas’s snapshot of October 15, 2026, United States.
notes: Grades: Documented, on the public record; Well supported, strong research evidence; Plausible, some evidence; Contested, evidence disputed. A claim’s grade covers that claim alone.

“Voice, power and information” has the smallest share of documented claims, 67.2 percent, and the largest share of plausible claims, 18.8 percent. “Work and financial security” has the largest share contested, 8.2 percent.
alt: Five panels, one per topic hub, show the share of each hub’s claims at each evidence grade. Documented claims lead in every hub, from 84.5 percent in public services where you live and 77.9 in cost of living to 67.2 in voice, power and information.
